title: Type every open mission blocker from retained facts and the engine's own rule, on greg blockers, the morning report and Mission Control
problem: Directive section 29 says: 'Blocked goals remain durable. Store: blocker, why blocked, reconsideration condition, required evidence, required authority, next possible move.' At base b1950be2 the engine keeps each blocker on the journal (mission.blocked, mission.unblocked) and decides when it lifts (MissionEngine._blocker_resolved), but no founder surface states the six fields. An outage back-off appears on status.active_constraint (as lifted_by: "outage"), on morning q4 and on morning q13, and none of the three carries a required authority (probe docs/evidence/typed-blockers-2026-10-30/outage_surfaces.py). A spend stop is visible only as an ask. The founder cannot read, in one place, who must act on a blocked goal and with what.
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE (directive sections 29 PERSISTENT OPERATION: 'Blocked goals remain durable. Store: ...'; 30 NIGHT SHIFT / MORNING TRIBUNAL: the morning review answers 'what intentionally was not done' and 'what requires founder judgment'; 70 REQUIRED QUESTION; recorded by #227, now on #196's head 4dc0d581, not in this branch's base b1950be2)
INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN (build the whole directive first; the founder-device run comes after, as its acceptance; recorded by #227)

INTENT-20261019-UPWARD-ASCENT (existing mechanisms, MissionBook, _blocker_resolved, active_constraint's withdrawn and paused_by markers, body_pauses, and the appraiser's read-only registry view, are composed into a capability none had alone; this is integration, not invention)
baseline: b1950be2 (#196's head when the unit started): blockers live on the journal and in the MissionBook; missions.active_constraint gives greg status a blocker with lifted_by (for an outage, the string "outage"); the morning report has no blockers section; Mission Control has no blocked-goals table; greg decisions lists founder asks only. No surface names the required evidence or required authority for every blocker kind.

alternatives.name: Proposed: a read-only projection, greg/blockers.py, on three founder surfaces
alternatives.description: Fold the journal through the one MissionBook; ask MissionEngine._blocker_resolved (on the running engine, or on a read-only engine over registry_view plus Genesis.restore(record=False)) whether each blocker still holds; type each one as {mission_id, kind, blocker, why, reconsider_when, required_evidence, required_authority, next_move, since, source_event}, every field non-empty text, 'none required: <reason>' where a field does not apply, BlockerError for an incomplete record. Reuse active_constraint's withdrawn marker and its paused_by over body.body_pauses so holds lead each record. Surfaces: `greg blockers [--mission ID]` (one parser block, one handler), a guarded morning-report section (blockers.section: the records, or {unavailable, error}), and Mission Control's projection()['blockers'] with a 'Blocked goals' table.
advantages: All six section-29 fields for five of the six blocker kinds, on three surfaces, from one function
Listing follows the engine's own rule (a test monkeypatches _blocker_resolved to prove it is called, not copied)
No edit to greg/missions.py, greg/asks.py, greg/genesis.py, greg/body.py or greg/console.py; no new ledger record
Records, signs, attaches and asks nothing; never opens the secret broker (tested)
Founder surfaces stay up with the reason when the records cannot be computed
disadvantages: The fields beyond blocker and why are derived at read time, not stored at block time
Couples to a private engine method and to active_constraint's markers
Re-runs Genesis.restore(record=False) on each call; cost grows with formed capabilities (unmeasured on a large body)
An unpaused no_strategy blocker is never listed, because the engine's rule always treats it as resolved
Two added lines in greg/tribunal.py, which three stale open drafts (#115, #119, #121) also edit
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained as the proposal; revisit if the missions.py owner makes _blocker_resolved distinguish 're-evaluate at the next tick' from 'resolved', or if the founder reads 'Store' as a persisted record.

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: add the six fields to missions.active_constraint (greg status)
alternatives.description: Extend the blocker entry that greg status already shows with reconsider_when, required_evidence, required_authority and next_move.
advantages: One function, one surface already in use, no new module
Shares the withdrawn and paused_by logic by construction
disadvantages: Edits greg/missions.py, which the unit spec avoid-lists and open PRs #209, #228, #229 and #244 edit

alternatives.revival_evidence: After #209, #228, #229 and #244 land, the missions.py owner can have active_constraint adopt blockers.typed records instead of lifted_by='outage' (recorded follow-up).

alternatives.name: Strongest competing design: store the six fields at block time in mission.blocked
alternatives.description: Extend MissionEngine._block so each mission.blocked fact carries reconsider_when, required_evidence, required_authority and next_move, a literal reading of section 29's 'Store:'.
advantages: The text is fixed in the ledger when the blocker is raised; historical records never change with later code
No resolution rule re-run at read time
disadvantages: Edits greg/missions.py (avoid-listed; open PRs) and changes a ledger record format that other readers and digests consume
Text frozen at block time goes stale: a later pause, body hold, withdrawal or answer changes what the founder must do
Existing mission.blocked facts lack the fields and would need a read-time fallback anyway
alternatives.revival_evidence: A founder ruling that section 29's 'Store' means a persisted per-blocker record, or the missions.py owner adopting block-time fields after the open PRs on that file land.

roles.position: Section 29 asks that a blocked goal stay durable with six named fields. The blocker and its reason are already stored on the one journal; this unit derives the other four from those stored facts and the engine's own rule, and shows all six where the founder already looks: the morning report (section 30), Mission Control and a dedicated command. Section 70's answer is concrete: for every pursued mission, GREG now states what blocks it, why, when it is reconsidered, what evidence and whose authority would lift it, and the next move. No authority is created; a record names who must act and grants nothing.
material_concerns: Section 29 says 'Store:'. Here four of the six fields are derived at read time from stored facts, not persisted at block time. This is a translation the founder may read differently
An unpaused, self-clearing no_strategy blocker is never listed, so such a stuck mission does not appear on the new surfaces; greg status still shows it
The console's /morning page (greg/console.py, avoid-listed) does not show the section; Mission Control's Goal Chase view does

Reality is UNIT-TESTED with integration-tested surfaces on in-process SANDBOX bodies with per-test keys; VEPMC stays 0, and per INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN the device run is the later acceptance
